doc.title: Neal Caine interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019

title: Drummers who ghost the bass drum
summary: Caine dislikes loud bass drum ghosting that clashes with the bass frequency.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: What would aggravate you on the bandstand?

Oh I could tell you what aggravates the hell out of me is when drummers play — when they “ghost” the bass drum. When they go [beats] but they do it real fucking loud so it sounds like a polka. And it gets in the way of the bass frequency. That irks me.
Well you know like drummers, you know like Sam Woodyard with the Basie — I mean with Duke Ellington. Sometimes drummers will lightly play quarter notes on the bass drum. Evidently —
Almost like they’re tapping their foot and their foot happens to be on the —

And evidently these guys did it but I never heard it, and guys do it and I never hear it, but a lot of — some drummers do it real loud and so it fucks up — it’s really annoying and distracting and it’s in the frequency of the bass and it makes it sound like an Army band. So I hate that. I don’t know if that’s what you were looking for.
That’s the first thing I usually like, “Oh God, get off the bass drum bro.” I go, “Get off the bass.” They go, “Well if you have a balanced drum kit you’re supposed to have” — yeah right. Please.
